summary: Builds small key-cap style labels that show a keyboard key, such as Ctrl or K, with a group wrapper for key combinations.
purpose: Lets the app show keyboard shortcuts visibly, often in menus or tooltips.
why: Likely reason: showing key names helps users learn shortcuts. The code does not state this directly.
how: It imports the style helper. It builds the key-cap style, with a color change when it sits inside a tooltip. It builds a group wrapper that spaces several keys apart. It exports both.
inputs: Text or key names placed inside, plus style overrides and standard element settings.
outputs: Visual key labels only. Nothing is stored and no shortcut is triggered.
risks: Display only. The group wrapper uses the same kind of element as the key cap, so nesting them can produce odd markup and screen reader output.
debug: If key caps look wrong, check the style in this file. If the group wrapper looks odd or reads oddly, check the element it renders.
